front: Give three names for God in indigenous belief.
back: Mwari and Nyadenga (Shona); uMlimo or Mwali (Ndebele).
Family ancestral spirits, believed to protect and guide their descendants.
Territorial or clan spirits of founding or royal ancestors, guardians of the land and linked to rain.
Alien or wandering spirits believed to give special skills such as healing, hunting or dancing.
The avenging spirit of a person seriously wronged; the wrong must be put right through compensation and reconciliation.
A person through whom a spirit is believed to speak to the living.
In the Matobo Hills; it is associated with Mwari/uMlimo and rain.

front: How do sacred places help the environment?
back: Bans on cutting trees, hunting or fishing there conserve forests, springs and wildlife.

front: How do indigenous religion and Christianity relate today?
back: Opposition from some, coexistence for many (following both), blending in African-initiated churches, and dialogue.
